title: Keep the desktop responsive during AUR source builds
head: 9a2d3e468ac8
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A saved yay makepkgconf does not take precedence, it is overwritten by the command-line temporary config
leads.consequence: When the system makepkg.conf is readable, yay v13.0.1 loads its saved makepkgconf first, then ParseCommandLine assigns the supplied --makepkgconf to the SAME configuration field. Its BuildMakepkgCmd passes that new value as makepkg --config. A user who configured a separate makepkg config in yay loses its settings for omarchy update, contrary to the new comment. The previous yay -Sua call did not override the saved path; the next Omarchy update does so again. Honor that saved path or document this actual override and decide explicitly whether to enforce the cap in it.

leads.summary: Configs using MAKEPKG_CONF to find their own includes break under the wrapper
leads.consequence: makepkg 7.1.0 assigns MAKEPKG_CONF to the --config path before sourcing files. Thus a real config with `source "$MAKEPKG_CONF.d/extra.conf"` works directly but resolves to the temporary config's .d path when Omarchy supplies --makepkgconf. makepkg aborts before building the AUR package, yay returns failure and the updater exits 1; the next run repeats. Sourcing the original file does not restore the MAKEPKG_CONF variable. Use a solution that preserves the config's effective path in the makepkg sourcing context, or explicitly account for this incompatibility.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus; reproduced; published as low note

leads.summary: Unreadable makepkg drop-ins are ignored instead of aborting config loading
leads.consequence: makepkg 7.1.0 sources EVERY matching .d/*.conf, and source_safe exits on a source error; Omarchy conditionally emits only readable drop-ins. A matching mode-000 drop-in made direct makepkg return 6 with Permission denied, but the generated config returned 0 without reading or diagnosing it. If a required setting lived in that file, an AUR package could be built without it; this repeats until the file permissions are corrected. Emit each matched drop-in and let makepkg's existing source error handling run.

leads.summary: Temporary config creation failure still invokes yay and can report success without the job cap
leads.consequence: If TMPDIR is missing or unwritable, mktemp fails and leaves makepkg_config empty. The script has no errexit and does not check mktemp or the config write; it prints errors but invokes yay with no --makepkgconf and exits 0 if yay succeeds. With a config that sets MAKEFLAGS=-j4 and override 1, makepkg is then free to replace the environment's -j1 with -j4. There is no retry or explicit failure, so every update under the same TMPDIR repeats. Fail before yay when the temporary config cannot be created or written.
leads.triage: follow-up to Opus; reproduced; not published (low realism)

leads.summary: Zero as a job-count override reaches GNU Make as invalid -j0
leads.consequence: The computed default has a floor of one, but the user override bypasses validation. OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=0 emits -j0 in the environment and generated config. GNU Make rejects it with 'the -j option requires a positive integer argument', so a PKGBUILD invoking make fails, yay fails and omarchy update returns 1; repeated runs with the same override fail. Reject non-positive/non-numeric overrides with an actionable error or apply the floor to the override too.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (optional note); published as optional note

leads.summary: The new test only inspects shell text and depends on the host's makepkg.conf
leads.consequence: The new tests are skipped altogether if their host /etc/makepkg.conf is unreadable (unless MAKEPKG_CONF is set), and run_updater then sets MAKEPKG_CONF to empty, so its default cases use the host config rather than a synthetic fixture. The stub yay only copies --makepkgconf and does not invoke makepkg or Make: mutations that drop an unreadable drop-in or break MAKEPKG_CONF-relative includes still satisfy every assertion, as the three boundary reproductions demonstrate. Provide a synthetic config for all cases and assert at least one real makepkg/Make consumer result and failure behavior; also assert argv if claiming to preserve yay options.

leads.summary: Open #11826's paru selection cannot be merged without reconciling this yay invocation
leads.consequence: Open PR #11826 routes the AUR updater through omarchy-pkg-aur-helper and adds a test selecting paru; #12778 still runs yay and adds yay-only --makepkgconf. Their heads diverge; git merge-file against #11826's actual merge base produces conflict markers around the updater call. If only this invocation survives manual resolution, someone selecting paru still updates with yay or has no AUR update if yay is uninstalled, and #11826's pkg-aur-helper test's expected paru line fails. Keep the helper selection and check the selected helper's accepted makepkg config options when resolving.
leads.triage: open PR #11826 overlap confirmed by Opus; not published

leads.summary: Open #9227's AUR confirmation is a competing edit to the same update phase
leads.consequence: Open PR #9227 inserts a user confirmation before rerunning third-party PKGBUILDs and skips when no TTY. Their heads diverge and merging the two updater files against #9227's actual merge base produces conflict markers. Choosing the #12778 side alone would drop #9227's noninteractive refusal and explicit confirmation, while choosing #9227 alone loses these job controls. Both behaviors need an explicit combined update/test if both merge; #9227 is reported CONFLICTING by GitHub against quattro.

leads.summary: Open #13474/#13646 implement opposite AUR-failure policy in the same invocation
leads.consequence: Both open PRs #13474 and #13646 introduce a writable Go module cache pass and replace `yay ... || exit 1` with a warning that returns success after a failed AUR update. Both heads diverge from #12778, and their own patch for bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs fails against #12778. Resolving by retaining the old `|| exit 1` loses their explicit policy; retaining only their yay line drops nice/ionice and the build config. Reconcile the invocation and choose failure semantics explicitly, including the new test's expectations.
leads.triage: open PRs #13474/#13646 overlap confirmed by Opus; not published

limits: #11826/#9227/#13474/#13646 conflict evidence is source/merge-file based, not a successfully merged full suite; manual conflict resolution has not been tested. Only source and the targeted bin-style test were run, not the complete CLI/shell suite. The new test itself was not run unmodified because it can source the host /etc/makepkg.conf despite a synthetic MAKEPKG_CONF being passed in, and the brief prohibits using host config as fixture. No posting to GitHub.

flags.why: Setting it only at the top changes source_makepkg_config's local MAKEPKG_CONF, so after the generated file returns makepkg re-sources the real drop-ins and (default path) the user file after the appended -jN, undoing the cap.
flags.fix: Set MAKEPKG_CONF to the real path before the source lines and back to the generated file's path before the MAKEFLAGS line; a review-only patch doing both kept the cap and found the companion file. Drop 'Not tested'.

flags.why: 'Stock' verified (Arch packaging makepkg.conf/rust.conf/fortran.conf at abdc0df and pacman etc/ templates have no MAKEPKG_CONF). 'Published' rests on one GitHub code search (MAKEPKG_CONF filename:makepkg.conf, 6 indexed hits, none sourcing through it) plus three related searches; GitHub search covers only indexed default branches.
flags.fix: Neither Arch's stock configs nor any makepkg.conf in a GitHub code search uses this form

flags.claim: With MAKEFLAGS=-j8 exported, or set in the system config or a drop-in, the updater correctly produces -j8 -j4
flags.why: True for system/drop-in settings. For an exported MAKEFLAGS, -j8 comes from merged_makeflags inheriting the caller's env (test 75-77); run_updater passes MAKEFLAGS= (test 61) and the real updater exports MAKEFLAGS=-jN (updater 63), so makepkg would see -j4 -j4. Also 'The test builds its merged config' should be 'the updater builds, the test evaluates'.
flags.fix: the evaluated value becomes -j8 -j4 (correct for a system or drop-in setting), but the test expects -j4 and fails

flags.claim: Suggested change: start from yay's effective value (yay -Pg | jq -r '.makepkgconf // empty') or skip --makepkgconf when one is saved; at minimum, fix the comment.
flags.why: Lost qualifier: not run as an updater patch (only the yay -Pg JSON output was verified). Dropped part: the PR description carries the same wrong sentence.
flags.fix: ... at minimum, fix the comment and the PR description. Not tested as an updater change.

flags.why: Not my suggestion and not run. By source it fits only the default-count checks (test 110-127): a non-default MAKEPKG_CONF makes the updater skip the user file (updater 49), which the spelling checks (test 83-108) rely on.

flags.why: The test file is new, so it never had one (it is the only one of 288 test/shell.d/*-test.sh files at head without one). 'every other file in bin/ on quattro ends with one' is correct (470/470). Same wording in my own report.

## Automated AI review > **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Outcome:** a yay-saved `makepkgconf` is replaced, although the new comment says it takes precedence. Follow-up at `9a2d3e46` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12778#issuecomment-5856697923). All earlier findings are resolved except the yay-saved `makepkgconf` part. ### A yay-saved `makepkgconf` is replaced yay 13.0.1 reads its saved settings before the command line, so the added `--makepkgconf` overrides a saved value; [lines 36-38](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/9a2d3e468ac8c7b3f571e3632fdce4e948338356/bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs#L36-L38) and the PR description say the opposite. **Impact:** `omarchy update` builds ignore a saved config. **Suggested change:** start from yay's effective value (`yay -Pg | jq -r '.makepkgconf // empty'`, not run) or skip `--makepkgconf` when one is saved; at minimum, fix both texts.
Reproducer (yay 13.0.1) # A makepkgconf saved in yay's configuration is replaced, not preferred The updater comment (bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs, lines 36-38 at 9a2d3e46) and the PR description say a `makepkgconf` saved in yay's own configuration "takes precedence over this override, so those builds keep yay's settings". yay 13.0.1 (the version in the Omarchy stable repository) does the opposite: the command-line `--makepkgconf` the updater adds replaces the saved value, and yay then passes the updater's file to makepkg as `--config`. Source (yay v13.0.1): `main.go` loads `config.json` (`settings.NewConfig`, line 70) and `init.lua` (`lua.Load`, line 88) before `cfg.ParseCommandLine` (line 101); `pkg/settings/args.go:133-134` sets `c.MakepkgConf = value` for `--makepkgconf`; `pkg/settings/exe/cmd_builder.go:145-147` passes `c.MakepkgConfPath` as `makepkg --config`. ## Reproducer Needs yay 13.0.1. Uses a throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `pacman.conf`; `yay -Pg` only prints the effective configuration and runs no package operation. ```bash #!/bin/bash set -eu t=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$t/db/local" "$t/db/sync" "$t/xdg/yay" printf '[options]\nRootDir = %s/\nDBPath = %s/db/\nArchitecture = x86_64\nSigLevel = Never\n' "$t" "$t" >"$t/pacman.conf" printf '{"makepkgconf": "/home/user/my-makepkg.conf"}\n' >"$t/xdg/yay/config.json" yay -V show() { XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$t/xdg" yay --config "$t/pacman.conf" -Pg "$@" | grep '"makepkgconf"'; } echo "saved in config.json:" show echo "saved in config.json, plus --makepkgconf as omarchy-update-aur-pkgs passes it:" show --makepkgconf /tmp/tmp.updater-config rm -rf "$t" ``` ## Actual output ```text yay v13.0.1 - libalpm v16.0.1 saved in config.json: "makepkgconf": "/home/user/my-makepkg.conf", saved in config.json, plus --makepkgconf as omarchy-update-aur-pkgs passes it: "makepkgconf": "/tmp/tmp.updater-config", exit status: 0 ``` The same happened when the value was saved with `yay --makepkgconf --save` and when it was set in `init.lua` (`yay.opt.makepkg_conf`): with the command-line flag, the effective `makepkgconf` was the flag's file in every case.
More findings (lower impact, reproduced at 9a2d3e46) ### An unreadable drop-in no longer stops makepkg Lines 46-48 write a `source` line only for drop-ins that pass `[[ -r ]]`. makepkg sources every `*.conf` in the `.d` directory and stops with `Failed to source` (exit 6) when one cannot be read. With a mode 000 drop-in, the merge base exited 6; this head built without the drop-in's settings. This contradicts the comment at lines 35-37. It is rare, since package drop-ins are normally 0644. **Suggested change:** test `[[ -e "$dropin" ]]` instead, so makepkg reports the unreadable file as before (a review-only patch did this and kept the PR's 10 checks passing). ### A `MAKEFLAGS` with a `--` section now breaks Make builds Line 57 appends `-jN` at the very end. For a configured `MAKEFLAGS="-j4 -- V=1"` (or `"-j4 --"`), Make reads the appended `-j1` as a target and stops with `No rule to make target '-j1'`. The merge base built with 4 jobs and `a873e0a3` with 1. Probably a rare spelling. **Suggested change:** insert the job option before the first standalone `--` when there is one, and append it otherwise (a review-only patch built every tested spelling with 1 job). ### Configs that reference `$MAKEPKG_CONF` now see the temporary file makepkg sets `MAKEPKG_CONF` from `--config`, so while the real system or custom config, its drop-ins and the user file are sourced, `$MAKEPKG_CONF` names the updater's temporary file. A custom config ending in `source "$MAKEPKG_CONF.local"` built at the merge base but made makepkg exit 6 at this head. This is the same class as the `BASH_SOURCE` case that was fixed. Neither Arch's stock configs nor any makepkg.conf in a GitHub code search uses this form, so it is a low-severity note. **Suggested change:** set `MAKEPKG_CONF` to the real path before the `source` lines and back to the generated file's path before the `MAKEFLAGS` line (setting it only at the top makes makepkg re-read the drop-ins and user file after the cap); a review-only patch doing both kept the cap and found the companion file. Or note the limitation in the comment. ### The new test fails when the host or caller already sets `MAKEFLAGS` The test builds its merged config from the host's `/etc/makepkg.conf` and drop-ins, and `merged_makeflags` inherits the caller's environment. When the system config or a drop-in sets `MAKEFLAGS="-j8"`, the merged config correctly yields `-j8 -j4`, but the test expects `-j4` and fails. An exported `MAKEFLAGS=-j8` in the shell running the test fails the same way, through the test's own evaluation only. **Suggested change:** run `merged_makeflags` with `MAKEFLAGS` unset and expect the host's configured value as a prefix, or assert the generated file's structure.

At 9a2d3e46, `bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs:46-48` writes a `source` line only for drop-ins that pass `[[ -r "$dropin" ]]`, so an unreadable drop-in is left out and the build continues without its settings. At the merge base 97a9fce5, makepkg printed these two lines and exited 6, and the updater exited 1: ```text /tmp/work/mp/lib/util/util.sh: line 108: /tmp/work/sys/makepkg.conf.d/30-private.conf: Permission denied ==> ERROR: Failed to source /tmp/work/sys/makepkg.conf.d/30-private.conf ``` At 9a2d3e46 the generated config had no line for the drop-in. `build()` ran, makepkg exited 0, and the drop-in's settings were absent. With `[[ -r "$dropin" ]]` changed to `[[ -e "$dropin" ]]` (not part of the PR; review-only patch), makepkg again exited 6 in the same setup, and the PR's 10 checks plus this block passed.
Reproducer: -- section in MAKEFLAGS # A MAKEFLAGS with a `--` section now breaks Make builds GNU Make reads the words after a standalone `--` in `MAKEFLAGS` as variable definitions or targets. At 9a2d3e46, `bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs:57` appends the job option at the very end, so for a configured `MAKEFLAGS="-j4 -- V=1"` (or `"-j4 --"`) the appended `-j1` lands after the `--`, and Make treats it as a target. Stop. not ok - a MAKEFLAGS with a -- section still builds exit status: 1 ``` ## End to end with real makepkg 7.1.0 and GNU Make 4.4.1 User config `MAKEFLAGS="-j4 -- OMARCHY_MAKEVAR=1"`, `OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1`, six-target Makefile run from `build()`: | Revision | `MAKEFLAGS` in `build()` | Make result | |---|---|---| | merge base 97a9fce5 | `-j4 -- OMARCHY_MAKEVAR=1` | 4 concurrent jobs, exit 0 | | earlier head a873e0a3 | `-j1 -- OMARCHY_MAKEVAR=1` | 1 job, exit 0 | | head 9a2d3e46 | `-j4 -- OMARCHY_MAKEVAR=1 -j1` | `No rule to make target '-j1'`, exit 2 | `MAKEFLAGS="-j4 --"` gave the same exit 2 at the head. `MAKEFLAGS="-j4 OMARCHY_MAKEVAR=1"` (no `--`) was capped to 1 job and built.
